prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM System; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry(BRR): thresholds, validation, reason codes, mode exceptions, connection/gate/towing/stand/swap rules, CTT window, freeze horizon, tie-breaker. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State(binding metering; RFM=Regional Flow Manager may suspend swaps); Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance State; Winter(MBO=Meteorology Briefing Officer confirms); Contingency Fallback State(ADM=Airport Duty Manager declares after RFM, Tower Supervisor, SSE=System Support Engineer). Fallback: Foxglove down→Digital Briefing Room; Marlinstone/CAM(Capacity Assessment Module) unreliable→last verified Airport Capacity Plan; Blueharbor down→Slot Coordinator manual sheet at Contingency Operations Console, keeps last CTT; revised CTT needs Tower Supervisor+Ramp Control Lead, AOC(Airline Operations Coordinator) readback; Ironleaf advisory; Emberline monitor-only; Regional Flow Platform reconciles with Collaborative Decision Log. Identity Access Service roles; least privilege; no shared accounts; separation of duties for GDP/AAR/Tactical Regulation Proposal; Silverpine emergency access needs incident ref+expiry. Audit Event Ledger logs auth, approvals, config, exports, emergency access, slot compliance, discrepancies. Tower Supervisor: Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Control Lead: Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor. PAW(Performance Analytics Warehouse): indicators, data quality, delay absorption (Demand Prediction Service, Slot Allocation Engine, Flight Data Exchange actuals), slot adherence vs CTT/TOBT, fuel/emissions factors. CAM records AAR baseline; AOC, Aircraft Operator Representative(AOR) challenge via Collaborative Decision Log. Data Governance Steward(DGS) measure provenance; MBO owns Weather Ingest Gateway; AOC owns schedule, TOBT; AOC/AOR submit Flight Intent Message. Training per role (Ground Handling Dispatcher: Handling Resource Planner; Slot Coordinator; Network Operations Liaison+Airspace Sector Planner: Sector Load Monitor, Common Situation Display; Emergency Response Coordinator). Exercises: multi-function, cover all mode transitions, log decisions/departures from proposals in Collaborative Decision Log; assess stale data, time sync, duplicates, conflicts, automation over-reliance; reviews use PAW+Audit Event Ledger. Human factors: workload monitoring, alert priority,

New part:
S895: Readiness Gate 2 shall confirm that the Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Weather Ingest Gateway can be connected without disrupting existing airport operations.
S896: Readiness Gate 3 shall confirm that local procedures have been mapped to the Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, and Arrival Regulation Console.
S897: Readiness Gate 4 shall confirm that training, shadow operations, contingency procedures, and operational acceptance criteria have been completed before live collaborative decisions are made through the Regional Flow Platform.
S898: Interface certification shall be performed separately from operational acceptance so that technical conformance defects do not become unresolved procedural issues.
S899: Each interface shall be tested for message structure, time stamping, identity attribution, replay handling, duplicate detection, outage recovery, and rejection behavior under degraded network conditions.
S900: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Gate Conflict Detector, Sector Load Monitor, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter shall be certified against agreed reference scenarios before they are used for operational recommendations.
S901: Certification results shall be recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log when they affect operational procedures and in the Audit Event Ledger when they affect access, configuration, or transaction traceability.
S902: Airport onboarding shall start with data discovery workshops that identify local tools, manual workarounds, unofficial spreadsheets, and locally maintained constraint registers.
S903: The migration plan shall classify each local tool as retired, retained for read-only reference, integrated through an approved interface, or replaced by a Regional Flow Platform function.
S904: No local tool shall be retired until the responsible operational owner verifies that its essential decisions, timing assumptions, and audit needs are supported in the target process.
S905: During shadow operations, local tools shall remain the authoritative source while the Regional Flow Platform produces parallel outputs for comparison by operational users.
S906: The cutover decision shall be based on measured agreement between local practice and Regional Flow Platform outputs, user confidence, defect closure, and demonstrated recovery from simulated failures.
S907: After cutover, local users shall enter operational decisions through the Airport CDM Portal and shall avoid reintroducing uncontrolled parallel records that undermine common situational awareness.
S908: The Contingency Operations Console shall be available at each onboarded airport before reliance on the Regional Flow Platform is declared for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, or Contingency Fallback State.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
